correctness.rationale: The complete fan rays are primitive tube sums by [1, Definition 6]. If a Demazure root has a nonsingleton distinguished tube, singleton inequalities force every coordinate nonnegative; the character zero-sum then forces the zero vector, contradiction. With singleton negative coordinate -1, integrality fixes exactly one positive +1 coordinate. Two-vertex tube inequalities force its negative vertex to be a graph leaf and its positive vertex to be the sole neighbor, while induced connectedness proves the converse. Distinct leaf neighbors cannot be leaves for connected order >=3, making Cox derivations pairwise commuting. The complete-toric Demazure group theorem and the absence of opposite roots imply the claimed \(\mathbb G_a^{\ell}\rtimes\mathbb G_m^{n-1}\). All 770 connected labeled graphs of orders 3,4,5 pass exact ray-inequality tests; these are finite regression tests only.

originality.rationale: The closest primary construction [1] gives the toric graph-associahedral fan but not a leaf characterization of all root subgroups or the full connected group. Nill [2] and Liendo--Lucchini Arteche [3] give the general root-group automorphism theorem; applying it to this family needs the separate graph-theoretic root classification proved here. Eur--Huh--Larson [4] gives the complete-stellar/star additive action and is explicitly acknowledged as prior art. The full family root classification, commutativity and reductivity dichotomy were not found in the materially inspected literature or indexed comparisons. The possibility of an unindexed equivalent result remains.

value.rationale: The family is geometrically canonical and includes graph-associahedral toric varieties of every connected graph. The result gives the full connected automorphism group and its unipotent radical, showing that all non-toric connected algebraic symmetries come from graph leaves. The reductivity criterion and exact dimension are structural graph-to-geometry classifications, not a trivial isolated numerical check; they apply to all sizes and graph types. The star instance is known, but the graph-wide exclusion of nonleaf symmetries is the meaningful new boundary.
